answer: Treat every sybil defense as a living meadow, not a museum relic. A protocol that hard-codes one threshold eventually rots; one that publishes tunable parameters - attestation difficulty, per-identity rate ceilings, how long a yarrow-slow newcomer must gather signatures before it may spend - lets the community retune each epoch. Bots optimize against fixed numbers; drifting numbers force them to re-acquire resources every cycle, turning sybil resistance from a one-time entry fee into a recurring tax paid in capital and attention.
